text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Thirty armed robbers raid Kiambu politician Njenga Karume's homestead and seriously wound his daughter before escaping with household goods and cash.
- Uganda is to hand over to Kenyan authorities more than 78 head of cattle stolen from Kenya during raids in the past three months.

- Monica Wangu Wamwere, mother of jailed political prisoner Koigi wa Wamwere, vows that she will camp at Nairobi Hospital where her son has been admitted, until the government allows her access to see him.
- A house-help poisons six members of a family over the weekend to facilitate a robbery.
- The World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF) are pressurising the National Cereals and Produce Board to reduce its staff by 1,000 people and cut existing silos from 96 to 44.
- Roman Catholic Cardinal Maurice Otunga hints for the first time that he may retire as head of the Roman Catholic Church in Kenya.
- Wheat and maize farmers in Uasin Gishu district (Rift Valley Province) plead with the government to double import duty on wheat, to protect the market for locally produced wheat.
- Following an appraisal by a financial consulting company -- the Uganda Development Bank is ordered by finance ministry to stop all lending and cease in-house expenditure until further notice.
- A three year agreement under which Kenya will pay "fair market rates" for electricity from Uganda ends a long-simmering quarrel between the two nations. ($1=56 shillings)
